Where is the line drawn, where buying time is seen as a bad thing? Not everyone has the free time due to work, but a lot of people want to stay competitive without spending any money which can become impossible in certain games. I understand that games need money to run, and that's why we need things like this to begin with.

From what I can tell, buying things that do not have a guaranteed improvement towards your performance seems moderately acceptable (card packs in Hearthstone, characters in MOBAs).

But in those same situations, there's a line drawn between how difficult those things are to get compared to payers.
Planetside 2 had this major problem where earning new weapons was near impossible to get without cash, with no guarantee that the weapon is any better than your old one. Hearthstone, on the other hand, could net you a pack every other day without paying; a pack of 50 cards is $60, which is about $0.60 for a day's worth of work.

So how much should an average dollar be worth? An hour's worth of time? A half hour? A minute? If you were to accept a plan where players could buy experience in relation to how much time they would spend, what ratio of time saved VS dollars spent would be acceptable?

Is local "couch" co-op dying? Why or why not?

I consider it dead unfortunately. The consoles are just so underpowered that they have to use every resource possible to get 60 frames at 1080p. They have nothing to spare to render the game twice in split screen. Unfortunately 60FPS and 1080p sell more than local co-op.

If the consoles can't run couch multiplayer then developers aren't just going to add it in for PC gaming.

I'm hoping that Gears bringing back couch co-op brings the market back a little because as of right now the "next gen" consoles seem to have killed co-op.

I have noticed a big push to performance and 1080p etc. I wonder if that's going to be a permanent emphasis, or if that's just the focus right now because of new systems. I'm hoping that as current gen gaming cools down, developers will go back to experimenting with different ways of gaming such as couch co-op. I've always felt that couch co-op is dying from lack of interest, but that its death is getting a big push from lack of availability. Couch co-op may not be as popular with the advent of online gaming, but I think more people would play it if it were more available. Unfortunately you're exactly right: it's a feature that devs are quick to drop because it costs resources and doesn't yield a lot of extra interest these days.

That said, there is still a lot of couch co-op going on in the Nintendo ecosystem, online co-op is still going strong, and there's still the occasional XBLA style game that includes it. Maybe it's not quite dead yet :)

One word: Nintendo.

Playing couch co-op Brawl with my girlfriend is incredibly enjoyable, I'd say more than twice as enjoyable than playing it alone (or probably on the internet, had the Wii still that capability).

Even awkward laptop co-op on Binding of Isaac: Rebirth is something I really enjoy.

Basically, if it is dying, I still think there is a market for it. I don't really think friends playing couch co-op is that great, a friend of mine wouldn't go to my house just to play a local co-op game. But being in a relationship is where local co-op really shines for me.

tl;dr I don't know if it is dying but I personally think local co-op can't be replaced because of the human factor, especially in romantic relationships where both partners game.

That's a great point. I think there is still a market for it also. To expand on your comment a little, I think that couch co-op also appeals to a growing market of people getting into casual gaming. Girlfriends and boyfriends and family getting into gaming for the first time. Online gaming has a slightly higher barrier to entry, and with gaming itself becoming more mainstream, people's gateway games are more often what they play at a friend's house or gathering, not needing a console with an online subscription.

I have also spoken to a close friend about this project, and they made a good suggestion that I also submit for your consideration.
